title: the Rajasuya
hook: Bhima and Jarasandha wrestle for days and nights; the captive kings walk free, and Jarasandha's son is put on his father's throne
carry: leave the other side something real

segments.voice: Yesterday: three guests in Jarasandha's hall at midnight, refusing his welcome. Your line was they gave their names, and their reason.

Jarasandha does one thing first. He has his son, Sahadeva, installed as king, so Magadha won't be left without a ruler. A king who holds other kings in chains still makes sure his own people will have someone on the throne. Then he takes off his crown, binds his hair, and steps out to meet Bhima. No armies, no weapons. Two men, bare-handed, and a crowd of citizens gathering to watch.
screen: `HIS SON MADE KING FIRST.` → `NO ARMIES, NO WEAPONS.` → `BHIMA AND JARASANDHA.`

segments.voice: They wrestle, the text says, without stopping for food or rest, day and night, for days on end. They grip and throw. They strike with arms and knees. At last Jarasandha grows tired, and pauses. Krishna sees it and speaks a word to Bhima, who takes it as his signal. He lifts Jarasandha high, whirls him around, and brings him down, and the king of Magadha dies. Here the story could turn into a conquest. It doesn't. The three go straight to the prison and open it. The captive kings walk out and ask Krishna, what can we do for you? His answer is small, almost polite: Yudhishthira wants to perform the Rajasuya. Help him. That's all. Then something smaller. Jarasandha's son, Sahadeva, comes out with his ministers, bowing low, offering gifts. The kingdom is theirs for the taking, and Krishna gives it back. He reassures the young man and installs him as king of Magadha, on his father's throne. Remember where Krishna's counsel pointed: before anyone could be honored, the kings in that prison had to go free. Now look at the order of what he did. Free the prisoners first. Ask them for nothing but help with a rite. Leave the defeated king's family their home. The Rajasuya is still to come, but here is one picture of what it's for, in Krishna's hands.
screen: `DAY AND NIGHT, BARE-HANDED.` · `JARASANDHA TIRES, AND FALLS.` · `THE PRISON OPENS.` · `THE SON GETS THE THRONE.` · then, large: `FREE THEM FIRST. GIVE THE THRONE BACK.`

segments.voice: Recall a time you came out ahead of someone, in an argument, a contest or a deal, and picture what you did next, and whether there was something you could have left them or given back. There's no need to grade yourself; just notice where the moment after winning sits in you. If you pray, hold that other person in mind for a few breaths; if you don't, simply wish them well.
The Rajasuya. Today, its road opens a prison, and asks the freed kings only for their help, and hands a fallen king's throne to his son.
Your line: leave the other side something real. Krishna handed a son his father's throne. Day seven hundred fifty-five, done.

howItsDone: In traditional Indian wrestling, kushti, wrestlers train in an akhara, and Hanuman and Bhima are honored there as patrons of strength.

chat.says: After Bhima beat Jarasandha, did Krishna take Magadha for the Pandavas?
options: No. He freed the captive kings and put Jarasandha's son on the throne.
Yes, he gave Magadha to Bhima as a reward for winning the fight.
No, he gave it to the freed kings to share among themselves as thanks.
chat.meaning: Krishna opened the prison, asked the freed kings only to help with the Rajasuya, and installed Jarasandha's son Sahadeva as king of Magadha.

notes: All paraphrase. The text gives a specific span of days for the fight; it was left out on purpose. Confirm 'day and night, without food or rest'.
Confirm that Jarasandha installed his son Sahadeva before the fight, and that he removed his crown and bound his hair.
Manner of death: written as lifted, whirled and brought down. Popular retellings have Bhima tearing him in two; confirm Ganguli's wording and adjust if needed.
Confirm Krishna prompts Bhima when Jarasandha tires; the line is paraphrased loosely ('now').
Confirm the freed kings ask what they can do, Krishna asks only that they help Yudhishthira's Rajasuya, and Krishna installs Sahadeva.
Confirm that citizens gathered to watch the fight.
